No more shaking. - Or rather, of course the machine still shakes, but it doesn't transmit to the floors and nearby objects. Our laundry room sits upstairs so it concerns me when you can see bookshelves in other rooms shaking everytime the washing machine goes into high spin. What would that do to the structural lumber and joints in the long run I can only imagine. But now even the dryer to the right doesn't catch the vibration. It's definitely worth the elbow grease putting these things in place.

*edit* 8 months later...
Alright, these pads may only be a temporary fix. You may have to find the real cause and fix that, instead of relying on these long-term. About a year ago our machine started to vibrate audibly/visibly whereas we never had a problem with it or the previous one before. Adding these had helped dampened the vibration to the rest of the house, but fact is, the machine itself was still shaking. Now 8 months from the time I installed these pads the machine progressed to shaking even more violently than it used to. I have a feeling it's our sagging 20 yr-old wood floors which triggered the vibration in the first place, and continual usage in that condition had ground down the machine (8 yr old at the time of its final demise).

Poorly Designed - Save your money. The concept is appealing - "get those pesky coffee grounds into those reusable K-cups without making a huge mess." The sad part is, this COULD have been an awesome product if it were designed properly. Even worse, I have the mechanical aptitude of an eggplant, and even I can see the design flaw. Here's the concept: stick this device into the bag of coffee grounds, grab a scoopful with the closed end, and close the funnel end on top of it. Then stick your K-cup on top of the funnel, turn the device and K-cup upside down, and the grounds go neatly into the K-cup. Not rocket science, right? Unfortunately, the stem has a "male" ridge on the funnel side, and a "female" groove on the closed scoop side to keep the scoop and funnel aligned. What happens is the coffee grounds get into the groove when you scoop up the coffee grounds, and when you turn the device upside down to put the grounds into your K-cup, the grounds in the groove get released all over your work surface. So you've spent about $10, and you STILL have a mess. Had the groove been on the funnel side and the ridge on the scoop side, it would work fine. For me, a set of oblong measuring spoons from the dollar store does the job far more effectively and neatly. What to do with this? Maybe I can use it to harvest the doggie-doo from my chihuahua off my lawn. It sure doesn't work for transferring coffee grounds from the bag to the K-cup.
